Rashi on Yevamot 6b:10:1.english: And these [things] shall be for you - This is written regarding execution by the court in the section of murderers.

Rashi on Yevamot 6b:10:2.hebrew: ה"ג: מה מושבות האמורים להלן, במיתת ב"ד הכתוב מדבר — אף כאן כו':
Rashi on Yevamot 6b:10:2.english: This is the reading: Just as “habitations” stated below, Scripture speaks of court-imposed execution — so too here, etc.

Rashi on Yevamot 6b:12:1.hebrew: מאי לאו ר' נתן היא - דאמר הבערה אב מלאכה היא ובכרת, ואפ"ה, אי לאו דאשמועינן, ה"א: אתי עשה דוהומת ודחי ליה:
Rashi on Yevamot 6b:12:1.english: What, is it not Rabbi Natan - Who said [that] kindling is a primary category of labor and [punishable] by karet; and even so, if [the verse] had not taught us [otherwise], I would have said: The positive commandment of “and he shall be put to death” comes and overrides it.

Rashi on Yevamot 6b:14:1.hebrew: פתילה - של אבר — מתיך וזורקה לתוך פיו, ויורדת לתוך מעיו. והאי בישול גמור הוא, ואב מלאכה הוא — דממשכן ילפינן, ובישול סמנין היה במלאכת המשכן לצבע תכלת ותולעת שני:
Rashi on Yevamot 6b:14:1.english: A wick - [Made] of lead — one melts [it] and casts it into his mouth, and it descends into his innards. And this is complete cooking, and it is a primary category of labor — for we derive [the labors] from the Tabernacle, and the cooking of dyes was [present] in the work of the Tabernacle for dyeing sky-blue wool and scarlet wool.

Rashi on Yevamot 6b:16:1.hebrew: אמר רב שימי האי תנא - דאיצטריך דנסיב לה קרא למיסר מיתת בית דין בשבת, לאו משום דאי לא דאשמועינן, ה"א דחיא משום טעמא דעשה דחי, אלא משום דהוה מייתי ליה בקל וחומר דדחי שבת:
Rashi on Yevamot 6b:16:1.english: Rav Shimi said: This tanna - [The reason] that it was necessary for him to cite a verse to prohibit court-imposed execution on Shabbat is not because, had [the verse] not informed us, we would have said that it overrides [Shabbat] on the grounds that a positive [commandment] overrides [a negative commandment]; rather, because he would have derived by an a fortiori inference that it overrides Shabbat.

Rashi on Yevamot 6b:1:1.english: You do not revere Shabbat - For reverence is not written regarding it.

Rashi on Yevamot 6b:2:1.english: His money belt - A purse with which he girds his waist.

Rashi on Yevamot 6b:2:2.hebrew: קפנדריא - לקצר הילוכו, שלא להקיף, ויכנס בפתח זה ויצא בשכנגדו, ולא לשם עבודה, אלא לעשות צרכיו:
Rashi on Yevamot 6b:2:2.english: A shortcut - To shorten his walk so as not to go around, entering through this entrance and exiting through the one opposite it; and not for the sake of [Temple] service, but to attend to his [own] needs.

Rashi on Yevamot 6b:2:3.hebrew: מק"ו - מפרש בברכות, בפ' הרואה (ברכות דף סב:): מכי אין לבא אל שער המלך בלבוש שק, שאינו מאוס — ק"ו לרוק, שהוא מאוס לפני הקב"ה:
Rashi on Yevamot 6b:2:3.english: Through an a fortiori inference - It is explained in Berakhot, in the chapter 'HaRo'eh' (Berakhot 62b), from [the verse], “For none may enter the king’s gate clothed with sackcloth” [Esther 4:2] — which is not repulsive, [and yet is forbidden] — [that there is] an a fortiori inference for spit, which is repulsive before the Holy One, Blessed be He.

Rashi on Yevamot 6b:4:1.english: What does the verse teach - Is it not already stated: “You shall not do any work”?

Rashi on Yevamot 6b:6:1.hebrew: ללאו יצאתה - לומר שאין חייבין עליה כרת וסקילה, אלא לאו בעלמא:
Rashi on Yevamot 6b:6:1.english: [It] was singled out as a negative commandment - To say that one is not liable to karet [excision] or stoning for it, but rather [it is] a mere negative commandment.

Rashi on Yevamot 6b:6:2.hebrew: לחלק - שלא תאמר: אינו חייב סקילה עד שיחלל שבת בכל מלאכות, לכך יצתה הבערה מן הכלל לחלק — מה הבערה מיוחדת שהיא אב מלאכה וחייב עליה כרת וסקילה בפני עצמה, אף כל שהוא אב מלאכה כו':
Rashi on Yevamot 6b:6:2.english: To divide - So that you should not say: One is not liable to stoning until he desecrates Shabbat with all [prohibited] labors [together] — for this reason, kindling was singled out from the general rule to divide [them]: Just as kindling is distinctive in that it is a primary category of labor, and one is liable to excision and stoning for it on its own, so too, any [labor] that is a primary category of labor, etc.

Rashi on Yevamot 6b:7:1.english: This is the correct reading: “And Rava said, etc.”

Rashi on Yevamot 6b:8:1.hebrew: מושבותיכם - בכל מקום שאתם יושבים, אפילו בחוצה לארץ:
Rashi on Yevamot 6b:8:1.english: Your habitations - In every place where you dwell, even outside the Land [of Israel].

Rashi on Yevamot 6b:8:2.english: It is an obligation of the body - And [it] is not dependent on the land, like diverse kinds, orlah, heave-offerings, and tithes.

Rashi on Yevamot 6b:9:1.english: Or is it not, etc. - [The Gemara] explains [this] below.

Tosafot on Yevamot 6b:10:1.hebrew: או אינו אלא אפילו בשבת - משום "מה לי חומרא רבה, מה לי חומרא זוטא". הקשה ה"ר יהודה כהן: היכא בעי לאוקמי רבי ישמעאל כר' יוסי דאמר "הבערה ללאו יצתה"? והא בפ"ק דשבת (דף יב: ושם) אמר דרבי ישמעאל קרא והטה, ואמר: "לכשיבנה בהמ"ק אביא חטאת שמנה" — אלמא דבהבערה יש כרת! ועוד קשה: דנהי נמי רבי יוסי היא, מ"מ אי לאו "לא תבערו" הוי אמינא דמיתת ב"ד נמי דחיא שבת, משום "מה לי חומרא רבה כו'", אע"ג דנטילת נשמה אב מלאכה הוא; וא"כ, כי כתב "לא תבערו", אצטריך נמי "עליה" באחות אשה דליכא סקילה, דלא נימא "מה לי חומרא כו'"? וי"ל, דבלא"ה פריך שפיר טפי:
Tosafot on Yevamot 6b:10:1.english: "Or perhaps it is only even on Shabbat" - [The baraita suggested this] because of [the principle]: "What does it matter to me whether [there is] a major stringency, [or] what does it matter to me whether [there is] a minor stringency?" Rabbi Yehudah ha-Kohen raised a difficulty: How could [the Gemara below] seek to establish [the baraita taught in the name of] Rabbi Yishmael in accordance with Rabbi Yosei, who said [that the prohibition of] kindling was singled out [merely] as a negative prohibition? For in the first chapter of Shabbat (12b and there), it states that Rabbi Yishmael read [by the light of an oil lamp on Shabbat] and tilted [it], and said: "When the Temple is rebuilt, I will bring a fat sin-offering" — which proves that for kindling there is karet! And furthermore, it is difficult: For even granting that it is [according to] Rabbi Yosei, nevertheless, were it not for [the verse] "You shall not kindle," one would have said that court-imposed execution also overrides Shabbat because of [the principle] "What does it matter to me whether [it is] a major stringency, etc.," even though taking a life is a primary category of labor [punishable by karet and stoning]. And if so, when [the verse] wrote "You shall not kindle," [why] was [the word] "upon her" [aleha] also needed regarding [the prohibition of] a wife's sister, where there is no stoning, so that we should not say "What does it matter to me whether [it is] a [major] stringency, etc."? And one can answer that without this [line of questioning], [the Gemara's own] objection [below] is even better.

Tosafot on Yevamot 6b:12:1.hebrew: טעמא דכתב רחמנא לא תבערו הא לאו הכי דחי - בסמוך מוכח דלא בעי למימר השתא: מדאיצטריך "לא תבערו" לאסור, מכלל דבעלמא דחי; דמפרש: דאי לאו "לא תבערו", ה"א דלידחי, כמו בכלאים בציצית, דמה לי חומרא רבה ומה לי חומרא זוטא, ואיצטריך "לא תבערו" לגופיה. וא"ת: וכיון דלגופיה איצטריך, אדרבה, נילף מהכא דלא דחי, דלא אמרינן "מה לי חומרא רבה מה לי כו'"? וי"ל: דלא מצי למילף אלא לאו שיש בו מיתה, כמו בשבת דאיכא סקילה; אבל לאו שיש בו כרת גרידא, התם אמרינן "מה לי חומרא רבה מה לי חומרא זוטא", וה"א דדחי לאו דכרת, כמו אחות אשה, ולא לאו דמיתה, כמו כלתו וחמותו, דלהכי לא הוה מקשינן להו אהדדי. א"נ: השתא נמי מדאצטריך, כדלעיל, ואין חושש על "או אינו". וכל סוגיא זו לא אתיא כר"ש, דלר"ש איצטריך "לא תבערו" לאשמועינן דמקלקל בהבערה חייב, דמדאסר רחמנא הבערת שריפת בת כהן, נפקא ליה בפרק האורג (שבת דף קו. ושם). אלא הך סוגיא אתיא כרבי יהודה, דחשיב תיקון תקוני גברא, כמו מילה וקריעה על מת. ורבי יוסי ורבי נתן נמי דלא כר"ש, דלדידיה ליכא למידרש ללאו ולחלק, כיון דאצטריך למקלקל בהבערה. ור"ש נפקא ליה לחלק מהיכא דנפקא ליה לשמואל בפ' כלל גדול (שבת דף ע.). ו אר"י: דאי ללמוד על מקלקל בהבערה לחוד קאתי, הוה ליה לאשמועינן במקום שאין מצוה בהבערה. וא"ת: והיכי דרשינן ללאו או לחלק, כיון דאיצטריך "לא תבערו" למיתת ב"ד דלא דחי שבת? וי"ל: דדרשינן מדכתיב "הבערה", דאי למיתת ב"ד לחוד אתא, ה"ל למכתב "לא תעשו מלאכה בכל מושבותיכם". וא"ת: נהי דהבערה דבישול פתילה לא דחיא שבת דהוי הכשר מצוה, רציחה עצמה — כשנתבשלה הפתילה מאתמול, או חנק וסייף — תדחה שבת מטעם "מה לי חומרא רבה מה לי חומרא זוטא"? ומיהו, למאי דיליף מק"ו, ע"כ לא אתי "לא תבערו" אלא לרציחה עצמה, דהק"ו עצמו הוא על הרציחה, דעל הרציחה כתיב "מעם מזבחי תקחנו", ו"לא תבערו" אתא לאפוקי הק"ו. (וי"ל: כיון דגלי לן דלא אמרינן "מה לי חומרא רבה מה לי חומרא זוטא" בהכשר מצוה, ה"ה במצוה עצמה לא אמרינן. א"נ (אפילו הכשר מצוה נפקא לן מדלעיל, ואם אינו ענין לפתילה תנהו ענין לרציחה עצמה, ע"כ). וי"ל: דבכל דוכתין משוינן מכשירי מצוה שאי אפשר לעשותה מע"ש כמצוה עצמה, כדתנן בפרק רבי אליעזר דמילה (שבת דף קל. ושם): "אם לא הביא", ובפסחים פ' אלו דברים (פסחים דף סט:): "כלל אמר רבי עקיבא כו'"; והכא באי אפשר לעשות הפתילה מע"ש, מדאצטריך קרא למעוטי:
Tosafot on Yevamot 6b:12:1.english: “The reason that the Merciful One writes: ‘You shall kindle no [fire],’ [is that] if it were not so, it would override” - Nearby [on 7a], it is proven that [the Gemara] does not mean to say at this stage that since “You shall kindle no [fire]” was needed to prohibit [execution on Shabbat], by implication generally [elsewhere in the Torah, a positive commandment] overrides [a negative commandment punishable by karet]; for [the Gemara later] explains that if not for “You shall kindle no [fire],” I would have said that it should override, just as in the case of diverse kinds [of wool and linen] in tzitzit, as what difference is it to me whether [a prohibition has] great severity or minor severity? And [thus] “You shall kindle no [fire]” was needed for its own sake [to teach specifically that execution does not override Shabbat]. And if you say: And since it was needed for its own sake, on the contrary, let us derive from here that [a positive commandment] does not override [prohibitions of karet], so that we do not say: “What difference is it to me whether [a prohibition has] great severity or [minor severity]”? And one can say [in reply]: That one could only derive [from Shabbat a prohibition] that carries the death penalty, like Shabbat, which carries stoning; but for a negative commandment that carries mere karet, there we would say: “What difference is it to me whether [a prohibition has] great severity or minor severity,” and I would have said that [a positive commandment] overrides a prohibition of karet, such as [the prohibition against marrying] a wife’s sister, but not a prohibition carrying the death penalty, such as [relations with] one’s daughter-in-law or mother-in-law, for which reason we would not have compared them to each other. Alternatively: At this stage too, [the Gemara infers that a positive commandment overrides generally] because it was needed [here specifically], as explained above [on 6b:10], and it is not concerned about [the objection] “Or is it not [rather even on Shabbat]?” And this entire sugya does not follow Rabbi Shimon; for according to Rabbi Shimon, “You shall kindle no [fire]” was needed to teach us that one who causes damage through kindling is liable, as from the fact that the Merciful One prohibited kindling for the execution by burning of a priest’s daughter [who committed adultery], he derives it in the chapter [entitled] HaOreg (Shabbat 106a and there). Rather, this sugya follows Rabbi Yehuda, who considers [execution] a constructive act — the rectification of the person, just like circumcision and rending garments over the deceased. And Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Natan also do not follow Rabbi Shimon, for according to him [Rabbi Shimon], it is not possible to expound [the verse] as [teaching that kindling was singled out] for an ordinary negative commandment or to divide [the prohibited labors], since it was needed [to teach liability for] one who causes damage through kindling. And Rabbi Shimon derives “to divide” from where Shmuel derives it in the chapter [entitled] Kelal Gadol (Shabbat 70a). And the Ri said: For if it came solely to teach regarding one who causes damage through kindling, [Scripture] should have taught it in a case where there is no mitzvah involved in kindling. And if you say: And how do we expound [the verse] as [teaching that kindling was singled out] for an ordinary negative commandment or to divide [the prohibited labors], since “You shall kindle no [fire]” was needed [to teach] regarding court-imposed capital punishment that it does not override Shabbat? And one can say [in reply]: That we expound it from the fact that it is written “kindling”; for if it came solely for court-imposed capital punishment, it should have written: “You shall do no work throughout your habitations.” And if you say: Granted that kindling for cooking the [leaden] wick does not override Shabbat because it is a preparatory stage of the mitzvah (hekhsher mitzvah); [yet] execution itself — when the wick was cooked yesterday, or [executions performed by] strangulation and the sword — should override Shabbat on the grounds of “What difference is it to me whether [a prohibition has] great severity or minor severity”! However, according to that which is derived from the a fortiori inference (kal vachomer), perforce “You shall kindle no [fire]” comes only for execution itself, as the kal vachomer itself is regarding execution, for regarding execution it is written: “From with My altar you shall take him [to die]” [Exodus 21:14], and “You shall kindle no [fire]” came to exclude the kal vachomer. ([And one can say in reply:] Since [the Torah] revealed to us that we do not say “What difference is it to me whether [a prohibition has] great severity or minor severity” regarding a preparatory stage of a mitzvah, the same applies to the mitzvah itself — we do not say [it]. Alternatively: [Even a preparatory stage of a mitzvah is derived by us from above, and if it is not relevant to [cooking] the wick, apply it to the matter of execution itself; end of quote.] And one can say [in reply]: That in all places, we equate preparatory stages of a mitzvah that could not be performed from the eve of Shabbat to the mitzvah itself, as we learned in a mishnah in the chapter [entitled] Rabbi Eliezer deMilah (Shabbat 130a and there): “If he did not bring...”, and in Pesachim in the chapter [entitled] Ellu Devarim (Pesachim 69b): “Rabbi Akiva stated a general rule, etc.”; and here, [it is a case where] it was impossible to prepare the wick from the eve of Shabbat, from the fact that the verse was needed to exclude it:)

Tosafot on Yevamot 6b:13:1.hebrew: לא רבי יוסי - ואו אינו דקאמר — משום דשבת עשה ול"ת (וה"ק: או אינו אלא אפי' מיתת ב"ד); א"נ, משום דשאני לאוי דשבת, דחמירי:
Tosafot on Yevamot 6b:13:1.english: "No, [it is] Rabbi Yosei" - And [as for] the "or is it not" that [the baraita] states — [it is] because Shabbat is [both] a positive and a negative commandment (and this is what it is saying: "Or is it not [the case that execution overrides, but] rather even court execution [is forbidden on Shabbat]?"). Alternatively, [it is] because the negative prohibitions of Shabbat are different, as they are stringent.

Tosafot on Yevamot 6b:7:1.hebrew: מושבות דכתב רחמנא למה לי - והא דדרשינן בפ"ק דשבת (דף כ.): "בכל מושבות אי אתה מבעיר, אבל אתה מבעיר במדורת בית המוקד" — היינו משום דהוי ליה למכתב "מושבות", וכתיב "מושבותיכם"; ומדלא כתיב "לא תבערו לכם" וכתב "מושבות", משמע דאתא לכדהכא. ובסוף פ"ק דקידושין (דף לז: ושם), דקאמר: "מושבות דכתב רחמנא גבי שבת ל"ל? סד"א: הואיל ובענין דמועדות כתיב, ליבעי בה קידוש ב"ד כמועדות" — לא מדלא תבערו אש בכל מושבותיכם קדריש, אלא מקרא אחרינא דאמור אל הכהנים, דכתיב: "שבת היא לה' בכל מושבותיכם", דההוא קרא בענינא דמועד כתיב:
Tosafot on Yevamot 6b:7:1.english: "Why do I need 'habitations' that the Merciful One wrote?" - And as for that which we expound in the first chapter of Shabbat (20a): "In all habitations you may not kindle, but you may kindle in the hearth of the Chamber of the Hearth" — that is because it could have written "habitations," but it wrote "your habitations"; and since it did not write "You shall not kindle for yourselves" and [instead] wrote "habitations," this indicates that it comes for that which is [derived] here. And [as for] that which [the Gemara] says at the end of the first chapter of Kiddushin (37b and there): "Why do I need 'habitations' that the Merciful One wrote regarding Shabbat? It might enter your mind to say: Since it is written in the context of the Festivals, it should require sanctification by the court like the Festivals [therefore the verse is needed]" — it is not expounding from "You shall not kindle fire throughout your habitations" [Exodus 35:3], but rather from another verse, in [the portion of] Emor El HaKohanim, where it is written: "It is a Shabbat to the Lord in all your habitations" [Leviticus 23:3], for that verse is written in the context of the Festivals.
